Codex review: blocked before merge. ## What this changes This PR updates dependencies across OpenClaw and adapts existing build, packaging, and Muse approval handling to their newer contracts. **Example:** Building updater compatibility bridges with tsdown 0.23.2. - **Before:** The bridge generator recognizes //#region source labels but misses Rolldown's new // src/daemon/inspect.ts labels. - **After:** Both label formats resolve through the existing source-and-symbol ownership checks. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | Useful maintenance with focused supporting regressions, but two source-verified compatibility defects prevent a passing review. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | This maintainer-authored PR is outside the ordinary contributor proof gate; its body reports installed wrapper/AOT and Chromium/OOPIF qualification while explicitly leaving native application builds to platform CI. | | **Patch quality** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | 2 actionable review findings remain. | ## Product **Kind:** Maintenance · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Users and developers miss maintained upstream fixes when compatible dependency updates remain unqualified. **Reason:** Maintainer authorship establishes direction, and synchronized pins, preserved patches, and focused consumer adaptations provide useful maintenance. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 4 items remain** Keep open: this useful maintainer-authored dependency refresh has two concrete compatibility defects that block merge. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `cffddb96f728bd8d55558f35a35ecf2f5242ade9` ## Before merge - [ ] **Retain the qualified npm pin until its bundle is admitted (P2)** - Selecting npm 12.2.1 leaves the root npm-lock generator unable to validate its bundled dependencies. Its verified published tarball contains minimatch 10.2.5 and ip-address 10.7.2, while workspace overrides require 10.2.6 and 10.7.4. NPM_BUNDLED_DEPENDENCY_POLICIES still ends at 12.2.0, so neither the narrow bundle exceptions nor tarball-backed lock verification applies. The current-head check-npm-lock job also fails. Restore 12.2.0 and its lock entry, or qualify 12.2.1 through the existing exact-bundle policy without weakening validation. - [ ] **Update picker fixtures for client viewport measurements (P2)** - virtual-core 3.19.7 changes observeElementRect from offsetWidth/offsetHeight to clientWidth/clientHeight. The shared installModelPickerLayout fixture still mocks only offset dimensions, leaving the simulated viewport at zero height; virtual-core consequently returns no virtual rows. This explains the current-head model-control failure expecting two options but receiving zero and the missing model-option elements across both UI shards. Update the shared fixture's client dimensions while preserving row measurement and cleanup, rather than changing production picker behavior or weakening assertions. - [ ] **Await maintainer action** - A release manager must review the changed release-check scripts under the enforced code-owner requirement. - [ ] **Explain or restore the original intent of npm dependency qualification** - ed4c9d4434495921bc42192fe724f9fd0d5d629b: The previous refresh explicitly deferred npm 12.2.1 because its bundled dependencies failed existing validation; this PR changes the pin without updating that owner. ## Findings - [P2] Retain the qualified npm pin until its bundle is admitted — `package.json:2445` - [P2] Update picker fixtures for client viewport measurements — `ui/package.json:38` ### Provenance - `npm dependency qualification` changes intended behavior without addressing why it exists (ed4c9d4434495921bc42192fe724f9fd0d5d629b: The previous refresh explicitly deferred npm 12.2.1 because its bundled dependencies failed existing validation; this PR changes the pin without updating that owner.)
Agent review details ### How this fits together Dependency manifests and lockfiles feed package installation and builds; build adapters preserve updater bridges, packaged browser artifacts, and plugin runtime contracts. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Dependency manifests] --> B[Locked upstream packages] B --> C[Build and source ownership adapters] C --> D[Published OpenClaw package] D --> E[Gateway and plugins] B --> F[Native applications] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Retain the qualified npm pin and update the shared picker fixture while preserving the existing patch and updater owners. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Published dependency contents and current consumers establish both failure paths, corroborated by current-head npm-lock and model-picker CI failures; no local execution was performed. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The shared label reader and narrow Muse adaptation fit existing owners, but dependency qualification must also cover npm's bundled-package validator and picker measurement fixtures. Full review comments: - [P2] Retain the qualified npm pin until its bundle is admitted — `package.json:2445` Selecting npm 12.2.1 leaves the root npm-lock generator unable to validate its bundled dependencies. Its verified published tarball contains minimatch 10.2.5 and ip-address 10.7.2, while workspace overrides require 10.2.6 and 10.7.4. NPM_BUNDLED_DEPENDENCY_POLICIES still ends at 12.2.0, so neither the narrow bundle exceptions nor tarball-backed lock verification applies. The current-head check-npm-lock job also fails. Restore 12.2.0 and its lock entry, or qualify 12.2.1 through the existing exact-bundle policy without weakening validation. Confidence: 0.98 - [P2] Update picker fixtures for client viewport measurements — `ui/package.json:38` virtual-core 3.19.7 changes observeElementRect from offsetWidth/offsetHeight to clientWidth/clientHeight. The shared installModelPickerLayout fixture still mocks only offset dimensions, leaving the simulated viewport at zero height; virtual-core consequently returns no virtual rows.
